extraction_scope: Worker-6 source-reviewed mechanism adjudication from primary results, methods, figure captions, and supplementary figure captions; exact graph-point digitization was not fabricated.

mechanism_claims.entity_scope: OAK derivatives C12(omega7)X, C10X, C12X and comparator polymyxin B
mechanism_claims.claim_text: The paper supports an outer-membrane permeabilization mechanism context: E. coli ML-35p outer membrane became permeable at sub-MIC OAK values, with C10X described as more potent than C12(omega7)X and equipotent with polymyxin B in the local source.
direct_assay_types: E. coli ML-35p outer membrane permeabilization using nitrocefin hydrolysis

mechanism_claims.limitations: Exact dose-response graph point values were not digitized; the claim is limited to source text/caption-supported relative potency and assay type.

mechanism_claims.entity_scope: OAK derivatives in E. coli ML-35p
mechanism_claims.claim_text: The local source reports that the tested compounds did not permeabilize the cytoplasmic membrane at the concentrations used, except that C12X was noted as more potent than its unsaturated analog.
direct_assay_types: E. coli ML-35p cytoplasmic membrane permeabilization using ONPG hydrolysis

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Dansyl-polymyxin displacement assays support LPS-binding context: OAK affinity increased with hydrophobicity but was lower than polymyxin B, with the text reporting about a ten-fold difference for C10X.
direct_assay_types: dansyl-polymyxin displacement binding assay with E. coli/P. aeruginosa LPS
mechanism_claims.limitations: Used as mechanism context, not as a full quantitative binding table.

mechanism_claims.entity_scope: rifampin or erythromycin plus OAKs against Gram-negative bacteria
mechanism_claims.claim_text: The primary and supplementary material support a reciprocal chemo-sensitization phenotype: sub-MIC OAK reduced rifampin MICs and sub-MIC antibiotics reduced OAK MICs, while delayed addition reduced the synergy.

mechanism_claims.limitations: Mechanism remains bounded to membrane-permeabilization/LPS-binding context plus phenotype; no RNA polymerase interaction assay is claimed for OAKs.
